course_title: Practice Exam for Certified Scrum Master (CSM) Certification
note: English bank (20/11/2026, drafted by Claude, reviewed by Tuấn): 5 skills x 20 questions = 100 (each skill: 14 MCQ = 7 recognize + 7 understand, 6 essays = 4 easy + 2 advanced) + 15 knowledge chunks. Content follows the Scrum Guide 2020 and the Agile Manifesto. Skills CSM / Scrum Alliance / Certification are mapped to the Scrum framework, empiricism + values + Scrum Alliance, and the CSM exam. CSM exam facts (50 questions, 60 minutes, 37 to pass, renewal every 2 years, SEUs) are 'as of 2026' and must be re-checked on scrumalliance.org. Load with: python -m scripts.seed_review --file data/review/course_743_en.json

chunks.title: The four values of the Agile Manifesto
chunks.content: The Manifesto for Agile Software Development was written in 2001 by seventeen software practitioners. It states four values: individuals and interactions over processes and tools; working software over comprehensive documentation; customer collaboration over contract negotiation; and responding to change over following a plan. The manifesto adds that while there is value in the items on the right, the items on the left are valued more. So agile teams still use processes, documents, contracts and plans, but people, working results, collaboration and the ability to change come first.

chunks.title: Key principles behind the Agile Manifesto
chunks.content: The manifesto has twelve principles. The highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software. Changing requirements are welcome, even late in development. Working software is delivered frequently, from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, with a preference for the shorter timescale. Business people and developers must work together daily throughout the project. The most efficient and effective way to share information with and within a team is a face-to-face conversation. Working software is the primary measure of progress. Agile processes promote a sustainable pace: everyone should be able to keep a constant pace indefinitely, without long hours or overtime, because tired people make mistakes. Simplicity, the art of maximizing the amount of work not done, is essential. The best results come from self-organizing teams, and at regular intervals the team reflects on how to become more effective and adjusts its behavior.

chunks.title: Agile compared with Waterfall
chunks.content: In a Waterfall project, the work moves through sequential phases: requirements, design, build, test and release. The requirements are fixed at the start, and each phase finishes before the next one begins, so testing and customer feedback come late, near the end. Changing requirements late in a Waterfall project is expensive and hard. Agile works iteratively and incrementally: the team works in short iterations, delivers a small working increment in each one, gets early feedback from the customer and adapts the plan. Agile is a better fit when requirements are uncertain or likely to change; Waterfall can work when the requirements are stable and well understood.

chunks.title: The Scrum Master: a true leader who serves
chunks.content: The Scrum Master is accountable for establishing Scrum as defined in the Scrum Guide, by helping everyone understand Scrum theory and practice, both within the Scrum Team and the organization. The Scrum Master is also accountable for the Scrum Team's effectiveness. The Scrum Guide calls Scrum Masters true leaders who serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization. A Scrum Master is not a traditional project manager: the Developers are self-managing and decide who does what, when and how, so the Scrum Master leads by serving, coaching and helping others succeed, not by giving orders or assigning tasks.

chunks.title: How the Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team
chunks.content: The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team in several ways: coaching the team members in self-management and cross-functionality; helping the Scrum Team focus on creating high-value Increments that meet the Definition of Done; causing the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress; and ensuring that all Scrum events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the timebox. For example, if the Daily Scrum keeps running longer than its 15-minute timebox, the Scrum Master helps the Developers keep it short and coaches them to discuss details after the Daily Scrum. If something outside the team blocks the work, such as a broken server owned by another department, the Scrum Master works with the people who can remove that impediment.

chunks.title: How the Scrum Master serves the Product Owner and the organization
chunks.content: The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner by helping find techniques for effective Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management, helping the Scrum Team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items, helping establish empirical product planning for a complex environment, and facilitating stakeholder collaboration as requested or needed. The Scrum Master serves the organization by leading, training and coaching it in its Scrum adoption; planning and advising Scrum implementations within the organization; helping employees and stakeholders understand and enact an empirical approach for complex work; and removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams. When stakeholders bring new requests in the middle of a Sprint, the Scrum Master helps them understand that new work goes to the Product Owner and the Product Backlog.

chunks.title: The Scrum Team and its accountabilities
chunks.content: A Scrum Team consists of one Scrum Master, one Product Owner and Developers. It is usually 10 or fewer people, has no sub-teams or hierarchies, and is cross-functional and self-managing. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team, and for effective Product Backlog management: developing and communicating the Product Goal, creating and clearly communicating Product Backlog items, ordering them, and making sure the Product Backlog is transparent and understood. The Product Owner is one person, not a committee. The Developers are accountable for creating the plan for the Sprint (the Sprint Backlog), instilling quality by following the Definition of Done, adapting their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal, and holding each other accountable as professionals. In short: the Product Owner decides what to build and in which order; the Developers decide how to build it.

chunks.title: The five Scrum events and their timeboxes
chunks.content: Scrum has five events. The Sprint is the container for all the other events; it has a fixed length of one month or less. Sprint Planning starts the Sprint and is timeboxed to a maximum of 8 hours for a one-month Sprint. The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog. The Sprint Review, a maximum of 4 hours for a one-month Sprint, is where the Scrum Team presents the results of its work to key stakeholders, they inspect the outcome and discuss what to do next; the Product Backlog may be adjusted. The Sprint Retrospective, a maximum of 3 hours for a one-month Sprint, is where the team plans ways to increase quality and effectiveness. Shorter Sprints have shorter events. During the Sprint, no changes are made that would endanger the Sprint Goal, quality does not decrease, and scope may be clarified and renegotiated with the Product Owner as more is learned. Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and only if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

chunks.title: The three Scrum artifacts and their commitments
chunks.content: Scrum has three artifacts, and each one has a commitment. The Product Backlog is an ordered list of what is needed to improve the product; its commitment is the Product Goal. The Sprint Backlog is made of the Sprint Goal (why), the Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint (what) and an actionable plan for delivering the Increment (how); it is a plan by and for the Developers, and its commitment is the Sprint Goal. An Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal; its commitment is the Definition of Done, a formal description of the quality the Increment must meet. Work that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be released or presented at the Sprint Review; it returns to the Product Backlog. If the organization has no Definition of Done, the Scrum Team must create one for the product.

chunks.title: Empiricism: transparency, inspection and adaptation
chunks.content: Scrum is founded on empiricism and lean thinking. Empiricism says that knowledge comes from experience and that decisions are made based on what is observed. Lean thinking reduces waste and focuses on the essentials. Scrum has three pillars of empiricism. Transparency: the process and the work must be visible to those doing the work and those receiving it; inspection without transparency is misleading. Inspection: the Scrum artifacts and the progress toward agreed goals must be inspected frequently to detect problems. Adaptation: if something is off, the process or the product must be adjusted as soon as possible. The Scrum events give regular chances to inspect and adapt: for example, the Daily Scrum adapts the Sprint Backlog, and the Sprint Retrospective adapts how the team works. Short Sprints give frequent chances to inspect results and adapt.

chunks.title: The five Scrum values
chunks.content: Successful use of Scrum depends on people living five values. Commitment: the Scrum Team commits to achieving its goals and to supporting each other. Focus: the team focuses on the work of the Sprint to make the best possible progress toward its goals. Openness: the Scrum Team and its stakeholders are open and honest about the work and the challenges. Respect: team members respect each other to be capable, independent people. Courage: team members have the courage to do the right thing and to work on tough problems. For example, a Developer who honestly tells the team that a task is harder than expected shows openness and courage.

chunks.title: Scrum Alliance and its certification path
chunks.content: Scrum Alliance is a nonprofit membership organization that certifies Scrum practitioners and supports the Scrum community. Its best-known certification is the Certified ScrumMaster (CSM). The Scrum Master path at Scrum Alliance goes from CSM to A-CSM (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster) and then to CSP-SM (Certified Scrum Professional - ScrumMaster). Product Owners have a separate path that starts with CSPO. The official CSM course is taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer (CST). Scrum Alliance is a different organization from Scrum.org: Scrum.org offers the Professional Scrum Master (PSM) assessments instead. (Rules as of 2026; always check scrumalliance.org, because they can change.)

chunks.title: Becoming a Certified ScrumMaster: eligibility and the test
chunks.content: To earn the CSM, you first attend a live CSM course taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer (CST): 16 hours of training, usually spread over 2-3 days. After the course you have 90 days and two attempts to pass the online CSM test. As of 2026 the test has 50 multiple-choice questions, a time limit of 60 minutes, and you pass with 37 correct answers (74%). After passing, you accept the license agreement and receive the CSM certificate in your Scrum Alliance profile. Because exam rules such as the number of questions, the passing score and the number of attempts can change, always check them on the official site before the test. (Rules as of 2026; always check scrumalliance.org, because they can change.)

chunks.title: Common traps in CSM exam questions
chunks.content: Many CSM practice questions test small details of the Scrum Guide. Common traps: the Sprint is one month or less, never longer; the Daily Scrum is for the Developers and is not a status report to the Scrum Master; only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and only if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete; the Sprint Backlog belongs to the Developers; Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity, not a Scrum event, in which items are broken down into smaller items and given more detail; there are no special 'hardening' Sprints, because every Sprint should produce a usable Increment that meets the Definition of Done; if the organization has no Definition of Done, the Scrum Team must create one; and the Scrum Master is not a project manager who assigns tasks.

chunks.title: Keeping the certification and continuing to learn
chunks.content: The CSM certification must be renewed every 2 years. To renew it, you earn Scrum Education Units (SEUs), one SEU per hour of continuing education such as courses, events or reading, and pay a renewal fee; for the CSM this is 20 SEUs and a 100 USD fee. After the CSM, a Scrum Master can continue with the A-CSM (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster) and then the CSP-SM (Certified Scrum Professional - ScrumMaster). A certificate shows that you learned Scrum and passed the test; it does not prove years of experience. Real skill comes from practice, reflection and continuous learning, in the same spirit of inspection and adaptation that Scrum teaches. (Rules as of 2026; always check scrumalliance.org, because they can change.)

questions.content: When was the Agile Manifesto written?
questions.explanation: The Manifesto for Agile Software Development was written in 2001.

questions.content: Which of these is one of the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
options: Comprehensive documentation over working software
Working software over comprehensive documentation
Following a plan over responding to change
Contract negotiation over customer collaboration
questions.explanation: The manifesto values working software over comprehensive documentation.

questions.content: In the Agile Manifesto, individuals and interactions are valued over what?
options: Customer collaboration
Working software
Processes and tools
Responding to change
questions.explanation: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.

questions.content: According to the agile principles, what is the primary measure of progress?
options: The number of documents written
The hours the team worked
The lines of code
Working software
questions.explanation: Working software is the primary measure of progress.

questions.content: According to the agile principles, how often should working software be delivered?
options: Frequently, preferring a shorter timescale
Once, at the end of the project
Once a year, after full testing
Only after all documentation is complete
questions.explanation: Deliver working software frequently, from a couple of weeks to a couple of months, preferring shorter.

questions.content: How do the agile principles treat changing requirements?
options: They are refused once the project starts
They are welcome, even late in development
They are accepted only with a new contract
They are moved to the next project
questions.explanation: Agile processes welcome changing requirements, even late in development.

questions.content: How is the work organized in a Waterfall project?
options: In short iterations, each delivering a small increment
Without any planning at all
In sequential phases: requirements, design, build, test, release
By letting the customer write the code
questions.explanation: Waterfall moves through sequential phases; each phase finishes before the next starts.

questions.content: What does the Agile Manifesto mean by 'we value the items on the left more'?
options: The items on the right must never be used
The items on the left and right are equally important
Only documentation and plans really matter
The items on the right still have value, but the items on the left matter more
questions.explanation: Agile teams still use processes, documents, contracts and plans, but value the left side more.

questions.content: A team works 60-hour weeks for months to meet deadlines. Which agile principle does this break?
options: Sustainable pace
Simplicity
Face-to-face conversation
Welcoming changing requirements
questions.explanation: Agile promotes a sustainable pace that can be kept indefinitely, without long hours.

questions.content: What does the principle of simplicity mean in agile?
options: Writing the shortest possible code
Maximizing the amount of work not done
Using only one programming language
Skipping testing to save time
questions.explanation: Simplicity is the art of maximizing the amount of work not done: build only what adds value.

questions.content: When is Agile usually a better fit than Waterfall?
options: When the requirements are fixed and will never change
When no customer feedback is needed
When the requirements are uncertain or likely to change
When the team wants to test only at the end
questions.explanation: Short iterations and early feedback let an agile team adapt to changing requirements.

questions.content: Why is a late change of requirements expensive in a Waterfall project?
options: Waterfall projects do not allow any testing
Waterfall teams never talk to the customer
Changes are free in Waterfall
The design and build are already finished, so earlier phases must be redone
questions.explanation: Each Waterfall phase builds on the previous one, so a late change means redoing finished work.

questions.content: According to the agile principles, how often should business people and developers work together?
options: Daily, throughout the project
Only at the start of the project
Only when there is a problem
Once per release
questions.explanation: Business people and developers must work together daily throughout the project.

questions.content: A customer asks for a new feature in the middle of a project. Which agile value supports changing the plan?
options: Processes and tools over individuals and interactions
Responding to change over following a plan
Contract negotiation over customer collaboration
Comprehensive documentation over working software
questions.explanation: Agile values responding to change over following a plan.

questions.content: What does the Agile Manifesto mean by 'while there is value in the items on the right, we value the items on the left more'? Give one of the four values as an example.

rubric.text: The items on the right are still useful, but the items on the left matter more
A correct example of one of the four values

questions.explanation: Model answer: It means the items on the right still have value, but agile teams care about the items on the left more. For example, working software over comprehensive documentation.

questions.content: Name two agile principles about collaboration and communication.

rubric.text: Business people and developers must work together daily
Face-to-face conversation is the most efficient way to share information

questions.explanation: Model answer: Business people and developers must work together daily throughout the project. The most efficient way to share information is a face-to-face conversation.

questions.content: Give two differences between Agile and Waterfall.

rubric.text: Waterfall uses sequential phases; Agile works in short iterations with small increments
In Waterfall testing and feedback come late; in Agile feedback comes early and often

questions.explanation: Model answer: Waterfall does the work in sequential phases, while Agile works in short iterations and delivers small increments. In Waterfall, testing and customer feedback come late, at the end; in Agile, early feedback comes often.

questions.content: What does 'sustainable pace' mean in agile, and why is it important?

rubric.text: A constant pace that the team can keep indefinitely, without long hours or overtime
Important because tired people make mistakes: it avoids burnout and keeps quality

questions.explanation: Model answer: Sustainable pace means the team works at a constant pace that it can keep indefinitely, without long hours or overtime. It is important because tired people make mistakes, so it avoids burnout and keeps quality high.

questions.content: List the four values of the Agile Manifesto and explain one of them with an example.

rubric.text: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Working software over comprehensive documentation
Customer collaboration over contract negotiation
Responding to change over following a plan
A sensible example explaining one value

questions.explanation: Model answer: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools. Working software over comprehensive documentation. Customer collaboration over contract negotiation. Responding to change over following a plan. For example, if the customer needs a new feature in the middle of the project, the team changes its plan instead of following the old plan.

questions.content: Compare Agile and Waterfall for a project where the requirements are likely to change. Which would you choose, and why?

rubric.text: Waterfall fixes the requirements at the start and then follows the plan
Changing requirements late in Waterfall is expensive / hard
Agile works in short iterations, so the team can adapt after each one
Choose Agile for this project

questions.explanation: Model answer: Waterfall fixes the requirements at the start of the project and then follows the plan. Changing requirements late is expensive and hard in Waterfall. Agile works in short iterations, so the team can adapt and respond to change after each one. For this project I would choose Agile.

questions.content: What is the Scrum Master accountable for?
options: Writing all the Product Backlog items
Assigning tasks to each Developer
The Scrum Team's effectiveness
Approving the project budget
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is accountable for establishing Scrum and for the Scrum Team's effectiveness.

questions.content: How does the Scrum Guide describe the Scrum Master?
options: The project manager who controls the team
The technical architect of the team
A tester who checks every Increment
A true leader who serves the Scrum Team and the larger organization
questions.explanation: Scrum Masters are true leaders who serve the Scrum Team and the larger organization.

questions.content: What should the Scrum Master do about impediments to the team's progress?
options: Cause their removal
Ignore them until the Sprint Retrospective
Add them to the Product Backlog as features
Report them only to senior management
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master causes the removal of impediments to the Scrum Team's progress.

questions.content: Who ensures that all Scrum events take place and are kept within the timebox?
options: The Product Owner
The Scrum Master
The stakeholders
The most senior Developer
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master ensures events take place and are positive, productive and kept within the timebox.

questions.content: How does the Scrum Master serve the Product Owner?
options: By deciding the order of the Product Backlog for them
By accepting or rejecting the Increment
By helping find techniques for Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management
By negotiating the contract with the customer
questions.explanation: The Product Owner orders the backlog; the Scrum Master helps with techniques.

questions.content: How does the Scrum Master serve the organization?
options: By hiring and firing Developers
By writing the company budget
By approving every release
By leading, training and coaching it in its Scrum adoption
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master leads, trains and coaches the organization in its Scrum adoption.

questions.content: In what does the Scrum Master coach the team members?
options: Self-management and cross-functionality
Following orders from a manager
Working alone on separate tasks
Writing detailed documentation
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master coaches the team members in self-management and cross-functionality.

questions.content: The Developers ask the Scrum Master to decide who should do each task in the Sprint. What is the best response?
options: Assign a task to each Developer
Coach the Developers to decide this themselves, because they are self-managing
Ask the Product Owner to assign the tasks
Cancel the Sprint until the problem is solved
questions.explanation: The Developers are self-managing; the Scrum Master coaches rather than assigns.

questions.content: The Daily Scrum always runs for 40 minutes. What should the Scrum Master do?
options: Extend the timebox to one hour
Cancel the Daily Scrum
Help the Developers keep it within the 15-minute timebox
Run the meeting and ask each person for a status report
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is timeboxed to 15 minutes; details can be discussed afterwards.

questions.content: How is a Scrum Master different from a traditional project manager?
options: A Scrum Master writes the project plan and assigns tasks
A Scrum Master owns the budget and the contract
There is no difference; it is a new name for the same job
A Scrum Master serves and coaches a self-managing team instead of directing its work
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master leads by serving; the Developers decide how to do their work.

questions.content: Stakeholders keep interrupting the Developers in the middle of the Sprint with new requests. What should the Scrum Master do?
options: Help the stakeholders understand that new requests go to the Product Owner and the Product Backlog
Tell the Developers to accept every request immediately
Add the requests to the Sprint Backlog without asking anyone
Cancel the Sprint so the requests can be done
questions.explanation: New work goes through the Product Owner; the Scrum Master protects the Sprint by facilitating this.

questions.content: The team is blocked by a problem with another department that it cannot solve itself. What should the Scrum Master do?
options: Tell the team to wait until the next Sprint
Work to remove the impediment, for example by talking to that department
Ignore it, because impediments are the team's problem
Remove the work from the Sprint Backlog without telling anyone
questions.explanation: Causing the removal of impediments is part of how the Scrum Master serves the team.

questions.content: Why is the Scrum Master called a 'true leader who serves'?
options: They are the most senior member of the team
They decide what the team builds
They lead by helping others succeed, not by giving orders
They approve every change to the plan
questions.explanation: Servant leadership: leading through service, coaching and removing obstacles.

questions.content: An organization is new to Scrum and its managers still expect detailed yearly plans. How can the Scrum Master help?
options: Ask managers to stop attending Sprint Reviews
Write a detailed plan for the whole year
Leave the problem to the Product Owner only
Help employees and stakeholders understand and enact an empirical approach
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master helps the organization understand empiricism for complex work.

questions.content: Explain how the Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team become more effective. Give two examples from real situations.

rubric.text: The Scrum Master establishes Scrum by helping everyone understand Scrum theory and practice
Example: removing an impediment that blocks the team
Example: keeping a Scrum event productive and within its timebox

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Scrum Master establishes Scrum by helping everyone understand Scrum theory and practice, so the team works better together. For example, when a broken test server blocks the Developers, the Scrum Master gets this impediment removed. Another example: when the Daily Scrum runs too long, the Scrum Master helps the team keep it within the 15-minute timebox.

questions.content: Name three ways the Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team.

rubric.text: Coaching the team in self-management and cross-functionality
Causing the removal of impediments
Ensuring Scrum events take place and stay within the timebox

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Scrum Master coaches the team members in self-management and cross-functionality. The Scrum Master causes the removal of impediments to the team's progress. The Scrum Master ensures that all Scrum events take place and are kept within the timebox.

questions.content: A Product Owner struggles to keep the Product Backlog clear. Describe three ways the Scrum Master can help.

rubric.text: Teach techniques for Product Goal definition and Product Backlog management
Help the team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items
Facilitate stakeholder collaboration (e.g. in refinement)

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Scrum Master can teach the Product Owner techniques for Product Backlog management and for defining the Product Goal. The Scrum Master helps the team understand the need for clear and concise Product Backlog items. The Scrum Master can also facilitate stakeholder collaboration, for example in a refinement session.

questions.content: Why is a Scrum Master not the team's manager?

rubric.text: The Developers are self-managing: they decide who does what and how
The Scrum Master serves and coaches instead of giving orders or assigning tasks

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Developers are self-managing: they decide who does what and how to do the work. The Scrum Master serves and coaches the team instead of giving orders or assigning tasks.

questions.content: During a Sprint, the Developers say that a broken database server owned by another department blocks their work, and the Daily Scrum keeps running over its timebox. Describe what a good Scrum Master would do.

rubric.text: Treat the server problem as an impediment and cause its removal
Work with the people outside the team who can fix it
Help the Developers keep the Daily Scrum within its 15-minute timebox
Coach the Developers to discuss details after the Daily Scrum

questions.explanation: Model answer: The server problem is an impediment, so the Scrum Master works to cause its removal. For example, the Scrum Master can talk to the other department to get help. The Scrum Master helps the Developers keep the Daily Scrum within its 15-minute timebox. The Scrum Master coaches them to discuss details after the Daily Scrum, so the meeting stays short.

questions.content: Describe how a Scrum Master serves the organization.

rubric.text: Leading, training and coaching the organization in its Scrum adoption
Planning and advising Scrum implementations
Helping employees and stakeholders understand an empirical approach
Removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Scrum Master leads, trains and coaches the organization in its Scrum adoption. The Scrum Master plans and advises Scrum implementations within the organization. The Scrum Master helps employees and stakeholders understand and enact an empirical approach for complex work. The Scrum Master removes barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams.

questions.content: What are the three accountabilities in a Scrum Team?
options: Product Owner, Scrum Master and Developers
Project Manager, Tester and Developers
Product Owner, Team Lead and Architect
Scrum Master, Business Analyst and Testers
questions.explanation: A Scrum Team has one Product Owner, one Scrum Master and Developers.

questions.content: What is the maximum length of a Sprint?
options: Two weeks
One month
Three months
Six weeks
questions.explanation: A Sprint has a fixed length of one month or less.

questions.content: What is the timebox of the Daily Scrum?
options: 5 minutes
30 minutes
15 minutes
One hour
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers.

questions.content: What is the commitment for the Product Backlog?
options: The Sprint Goal
The Definition of Done
The release plan
The Product Goal
questions.explanation: Product Backlog → Product Goal; Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal; Increment → Definition of Done.

questions.content: What is the commitment for the Increment?
options: The Definition of Done
The Product Goal
The Sprint Goal
The burndown chart
questions.explanation: The Increment's commitment is the Definition of Done.

questions.content: Who is accountable for ordering the Product Backlog?
options: The Scrum Master
The Product Owner
The Developers
The stakeholders
questions.explanation: Ordering Product Backlog items is part of the Product Owner's backlog management.

questions.content: Which list contains exactly the five Scrum events?
options: Sprint, Planning, Design, Testing, Release
Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Backlog Refinement, Sprint Review, Release Planning
Sprint, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Sprint Retrospective
Kick-off, Daily Scrum, Demo, Retrospective, Closing
questions.explanation: Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity, not an event; release planning is not a Scrum event.

questions.content: Who can cancel a Sprint, and when?
options: The Scrum Master, whenever the team is late
Any stakeholder who disagrees with the plan
The Developers, if they do not like the work
Only the Product Owner, if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete
questions.explanation: Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint.

questions.content: Who owns the Sprint Backlog?
options: The Developers: it is a plan by and for the Developers
The Product Owner
The Scrum Master
The stakeholders
questions.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers.

questions.content: For a one-month Sprint, what is the maximum length of Sprint Planning?
options: 4 hours
8 hours
2 hours
2 days
questions.explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed to 8 hours for a one-month Sprint.

questions.content: Which of these is allowed during a Sprint?
options: Lowering quality to finish faster
Making changes that endanger the Sprint Goal
Clarifying and renegotiating scope with the Product Owner as more is learned
Changing the Sprint length every week
questions.explanation: Scope may be clarified and renegotiated; quality and the Sprint Goal are protected.

questions.content: What does the Sprint Backlog consist of?
options: Only the list of bugs
All items in the Product Backlog
The Definition of Done and the release date
The Sprint Goal, the selected Product Backlog items and a plan for delivering them
questions.explanation: Sprint Backlog = Sprint Goal (why) + selected items (what) + actionable plan (how).

questions.content: What is the usual size of a Scrum Team?
options: 10 or fewer people
Exactly 3 people
At least 20 people
Any size; it does not matter
questions.explanation: A Scrum Team is small enough to stay nimble: typically 10 or fewer people.

questions.content: At the end of the Sprint, a Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done. What happens to it?
options: It is released with a warning
It is not part of the Increment and returns to the Product Backlog
The Sprint is extended until it is done
The Definition of Done is changed so that it passes
questions.explanation: Work that does not meet the Definition of Done cannot be released or presented; it returns to the backlog.

questions.content: Name the three Scrum artifacts and the commitment of each one.

rubric.text: Product Backlog → Product Goal
Sprint Backlog → Sprint Goal
Increment → Definition of Done

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Product Backlog has the Product Goal as its commitment. The Sprint Backlog has the Sprint Goal. The Increment has the Definition of Done.

questions.content: What is the Product Owner accountable for?

rubric.text: Maximizing the value of the product
Effective Product Backlog management (Product Goal, items, ordering)

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. The Product Owner is also accountable for effective Product Backlog management, for example ordering the Product Backlog items.

questions.content: What is the purpose of the Daily Scrum, how long is it, and who takes part?

rubric.text: Inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog
It is timeboxed to 15 minutes
The Developers take part

questions.explanation: Model answer: The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary. It is timeboxed to 15 minutes. The Developers take part in it.

questions.content: What happens in the Sprint Review, and what is its maximum length for a one-month Sprint?

rubric.text: The Scrum Team presents its work to key stakeholders and they inspect the outcome
They discuss what to do next and the Product Backlog may be adjusted
At most 4 hours for a one-month Sprint

questions.explanation: Model answer: In the Sprint Review, the Scrum Team presents the results of its work to key stakeholders, and they inspect the outcome of the Sprint. Together they discuss what to do next, and the Product Backlog may be adjusted. For a one-month Sprint it lasts at most 4 hours.

questions.content: List the five Scrum events with the maximum length of each one for a one-month Sprint.

rubric.text: Sprint: one month or less
Sprint Planning: at most 8 hours
Daily Scrum: 15 minutes
Sprint Review: at most 4 hours
Sprint Retrospective: at most 3 hours

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Sprint lasts one month or less. Sprint Planning takes at most 8 hours. The Daily Scrum takes 15 minutes. The Sprint Review takes at most 4 hours. The Sprint Retrospective takes at most 3 hours.

questions.content: Describe the accountabilities of the Developers, and explain how they differ from those of the Product Owner.

rubric.text: The Developers create the plan for the Sprint (the Sprint Backlog)
They instill quality by following the Definition of Done
They adapt their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal
The Product Owner decides what to build (orders the backlog, maximizes value); the Developers decide how

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Developers create the plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog. They instill quality by following the Definition of Done. They adapt their plan every day toward the Sprint Goal. The Product Owner decides what to build by ordering the Product Backlog to maximize value, while the Developers decide how to do the work.

questions.content: What are the three pillars of empiricism in Scrum?
options: Planning, execution and control
Speed, cost and scope
Transparency, inspection and adaptation
Design, build and test
questions.explanation: Scrum's three pillars are transparency, inspection and adaptation.

questions.content: What are the five Scrum values?
options: Speed, quality, cost, scope and time
Honesty, loyalty, discipline, obedience and focus
Planning, testing, release, review and feedback
Commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage
questions.explanation: The five Scrum values are commitment, focus, openness, respect and courage.

questions.content: According to empiricism, where does knowledge come from?
options: From experience and from decisions based on what is observed
From detailed plans made at the start
From the opinion of the most senior person
From long documents written before the work
questions.explanation: Empiricism: knowledge comes from experience and decisions are based on observation.

questions.content: What is Scrum Alliance?
options: A software tool for managing backlogs
A nonprofit organization that offers Scrum certifications such as CSM
A government agency that controls software projects
A company that sells project management software
questions.explanation: Scrum Alliance is a nonprofit membership organization that certifies Scrum practitioners.

questions.content: In Scrum Alliance's Scrum Master path, which certification comes after CSM?
options: PMP
CSPO
A-CSM (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster)
ITIL Foundation
questions.explanation: The path is CSM → A-CSM → CSP-SM. CSPO starts the Product Owner path.

questions.content: Which Scrum value means doing the right thing and working on tough problems?
options: Focus
Respect
Openness
Courage
questions.explanation: Courage: doing the right thing and working on tough problems.

questions.content: Which pillar requires that the process and the work are visible to those doing and receiving the work?
options: Transparency
Inspection
Adaptation
Commitment
questions.explanation: Transparency makes the process and the work visible.

questions.content: In the Sprint Retrospective, the team sees that testing is too slow and decides to automate its tests. Which pillars does this show?
options: Transparency only
Inspection and adaptation
Commitment and focus
None; the Retrospective is not about the process
questions.explanation: The team inspects how it works and adapts its process.

questions.content: Why is transparency needed for inspection?
options: Transparency makes meetings shorter
Inspection is only needed when transparency fails
Inspecting information that is not visible or not true leads to wrong decisions
Transparency removes the need to adapt
questions.explanation: Inspection without transparency is misleading and wasteful.

questions.content: A Developer honestly tells the team that a task is much harder than expected. Which Scrum values does this show?
options: Focus and commitment
Respect only
None of the Scrum values
Openness and courage
questions.explanation: Being open and honest about challenges shows openness and courage.

questions.content: The team works only on its Sprint Goal and avoids switching to unrelated tasks. Which value is this?
options: Focus
Courage
Openness
Respect
questions.explanation: Focus: concentrating on the work of the Sprint.

questions.content: What is the relationship between Scrum Alliance and Scrum.org?
options: They are the same organization with two websites
They are different organizations: Scrum Alliance offers CSM, Scrum.org offers PSM
Scrum.org offers CSM and Scrum Alliance offers PSM
Only Scrum Alliance is allowed to teach Scrum
questions.explanation: Scrum Alliance (CSM) and Scrum.org (PSM) are separate organizations.

questions.content: Why does Scrum work in short Sprints instead of following one long plan?
options: Short Sprints remove the need for any planning
They let the team skip testing
Short cycles give frequent chances to inspect results and adapt
They make documentation unnecessary
questions.explanation: Each Sprint is a chance to inspect and adapt, which supports empiricism.

questions.content: Who teaches the official Scrum Alliance CSM course?
options: Any Product Owner
The student's own manager
A Scrum.org Professional Scrum Trainer only
A Certified Scrum Trainer (CST)
questions.explanation: The CSM course is taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer.

questions.content: Name and briefly explain the three pillars of empiricism in Scrum.

rubric.text: Transparency: the work and the process are visible
Inspection: progress and artifacts are checked often
Adaptation: when something is off, the team adjusts quickly

questions.explanation: Model answer: The first pillar is transparency: the work and the process must be visible. The second is inspection: the team inspects its progress and artifacts often. The third is adaptation: when something is wrong, the team adjusts as soon as possible.

questions.content: Explain the Scrum values openness and respect.

rubric.text: Openness: the team and stakeholders are open and honest about the work and the challenges
Respect: team members respect each other as capable, independent people

questions.explanation: Model answer: Openness means the Scrum Team and its stakeholders are open and honest about the work and the challenges. Respect means team members respect each other to be capable, independent people.

questions.content: What is Scrum Alliance, and what Scrum Master path does it offer?

rubric.text: A nonprofit membership organization that certifies Scrum practitioners
The path CSM → A-CSM → CSP-SM

questions.explanation: Model answer: Scrum Alliance is a nonprofit membership organization that certifies Scrum practitioners. Its Scrum Master path goes from CSM to A-CSM (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster) and then to CSP-SM.

questions.content: Explain empiricism in Scrum, and give an example of adaptation.

rubric.text: Knowledge comes from experience; decisions are based on what is observed
A sensible example of adapting (changing the plan, backlog or way of working after inspecting)

questions.explanation: Model answer: Empiricism means knowledge comes from experience, and decisions are based on what is observed. For example, after the Sprint Review the Product Owner changes the order of the Product Backlog based on the stakeholders' feedback.

questions.content: A new team member asks how the Scrum values change the way a team works day to day. Name the five values and describe how each one shows in the team's behavior.

rubric.text: Commitment: committing to the team's goals and supporting each other
Focus: focusing on the work of the Sprint
Openness: being open and honest about the work and challenges
Respect: respecting each other as capable, independent people
Courage: doing the right thing and working on tough problems

questions.explanation: Model answer: Commitment means the team commits to its goals and supports each other. Focus means the team concentrates on the work of the Sprint. Openness means being honest about the work and the challenges. Respect means team members treat each other as capable, independent people. Courage means doing the right thing and working on tough problems.

questions.content: Explain the three pillars of empiricism, and show how one Scrum event uses inspection and adaptation.

rubric.text: Transparency: the work and the artifacts are visible
Inspection: checking progress and artifacts often
Adaptation: adjusting as soon as a problem is found
A Scrum event used correctly as an example of inspect-and-adapt

questions.explanation: Model answer: Transparency means the work and the artifacts are visible to everyone. Inspection means checking progress and artifacts often. Adaptation means adjusting as soon as a problem is found. For example, in the Daily Scrum the Developers inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog.

questions.content: What must you do before taking the CSM test?
options: Attend a CSM course taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer
Work as a Scrum Master for five years
Pass the PMP exam
Write a thesis about Scrum
questions.explanation: The CSM requires attending a course with a Certified Scrum Trainer before the test.

questions.content: As of 2026, how many questions does the CSM test have?
questions.explanation: The CSM test has 50 multiple-choice questions (check the official site, rules can change).

questions.content: As of 2026, what score do you need to pass the CSM test?
options: 25 correct answers out of 50 (50%)
45 correct answers out of 50 (90%)
37 correct answers out of 50 (74%)
50 correct answers out of 50
questions.explanation: You pass with 37 of 50 correct (74%), as of 2026.

questions.content: How often must the CSM certification be renewed?
options: Every month
Every 10 years
Never; it lasts for life
Every 2 years
questions.explanation: The CSM is renewed every 2 years.

questions.content: What do you earn in order to renew the CSM?
options: Scrum Education Units (SEUs)
Story points
Sprint credits
Exam tokens
questions.explanation: Renewal requires Scrum Education Units and a fee.

questions.content: Which of these is NOT a Scrum event?
options: Sprint Planning
Product Backlog refinement
Daily Scrum
Sprint Retrospective
questions.explanation: Refinement is an ongoing activity, not one of the five Scrum events.

questions.content: As of 2026, what is the time limit of the CSM test?
options: 15 minutes
3 hours
60 minutes
There is no time limit
questions.explanation: The CSM test has a 60-minute time limit.

questions.content: A practice question asks who must attend the Daily Scrum. What is the correct answer?
options: The whole company
The Product Owner and the stakeholders
Only the Scrum Master
The Developers
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is an event for the Developers.

questions.content: A practice question says that the Scrum Master can cancel the Sprint. Why is this wrong?
options: Only the Product Owner has the authority to cancel a Sprint
Sprints can never be cancelled by anyone
Only the stakeholders can cancel a Sprint
The Developers vote to cancel a Sprint
questions.explanation: Only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, if the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

questions.content: A team says it needs a 'hardening Sprint' to fix quality before every release. What is the Scrum view?
options: A hardening Sprint is a required Scrum event
Every Sprint should produce a usable Increment that meets the Definition of Done
Quality is checked only in the last Sprint
The Scrum Master decides when to run a hardening Sprint
questions.explanation: Quality is built in every Sprint through the Definition of Done; there are no hardening Sprints in Scrum.

questions.content: Why should you check the official Scrum Alliance site before taking the CSM test?
options: The exam questions are published there in advance
You must buy the Scrum Guide there
Exam rules such as the number of questions and the passing score can change over time
The site tells you which answers are correct
questions.explanation: Exam details can change; always confirm the current rules.

questions.content: You earned your CSM in November 2026. By when must you renew it?
options: By November 2027
By November 2036
It never needs to be renewed
By November 2028
questions.explanation: The CSM is renewed every 2 years.

questions.content: Which statement about the Definition of Done is correct?
options: If the organization has no Definition of Done, the Scrum Team must create one
The stakeholders write it after each release
Each Developer can use their own Definition of Done
The Definition of Done is optional in Scrum
questions.explanation: If there is no organizational standard, the Scrum Team must create a Definition of Done for the product.

questions.content: What does a CSM certificate prove?
options: That you have worked as a Scrum Master for many years
That you learned Scrum and passed the test; experience must still be built in practice
That you can manage any project without training
That your team will always deliver on time
questions.explanation: A certificate shows knowledge, not years of experience.

questions.content: Describe the steps to become a Certified ScrumMaster (CSM).

rubric.text: Attend a live CSM course taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer (CST)
Pass the online CSM test
Receive the CSM certificate after passing

questions.explanation: Model answer: First, attend a live CSM course taught by a Certified Scrum Trainer (CST). Then pass the online CSM test. After passing, you receive the CSM certificate in your Scrum Alliance profile.

questions.content: Describe the format of the CSM test as of 2026.

rubric.text: 50 multiple-choice questions
A time limit of 60 minutes
You pass with 37 correct answers (74%)

questions.explanation: Model answer: As of 2026, the CSM test has 50 multiple-choice questions. The time limit is 60 minutes. You pass with 37 correct answers, which is 74%.

questions.content: How do you keep your CSM certification active?

rubric.text: Renew it every 2 years
Earn Scrum Education Units (SEUs) and pay a renewal fee

questions.explanation: Model answer: You must renew the CSM certification every 2 years. To renew, you earn Scrum Education Units (SEUs) and pay a renewal fee.

questions.content: Is Product Backlog refinement a Scrum event? Explain.

rubric.text: No: refinement is an ongoing activity, not a Scrum event
In refinement, items are broken down into smaller items and given more detail

questions.explanation: Model answer: No, Product Backlog refinement is not a Scrum event; it is an ongoing activity. In refinement, the team breaks Product Backlog items down into smaller items and adds detail, such as a description, order and size.

questions.content: A practice exam states: 'The Daily Scrum is a status meeting where each Developer reports to the Scrum Master.' Explain why this is wrong, and describe the Daily Scrum correctly.

rubric.text: It is not a status report to the Scrum Master
It is for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal
They adapt the Sprint Backlog / their plan
It is timeboxed to 15 minutes and the Developers choose how to run it

questions.explanation: Model answer: The Daily Scrum is not a status meeting, and the Developers do not report to the Scrum Master. It is an event for the Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal. They adapt the Sprint Backlog and their plan for the next day. It is timeboxed to 15 minutes, and the Developers choose how to run it.

questions.content: Describe the Scrum Master certification path at Scrum Alliance after the CSM, how you keep it active, and why continuing to learn matters.

rubric.text: The next step is A-CSM (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster)
After that comes CSP-SM (Certified Scrum Professional - ScrumMaster)
Renew every 2 years by earning SEUs
Learning matters because the certificate is only a start; skill comes from experience and practice

questions.explanation: Model answer: After the CSM, the next step is the A-CSM (Advanced Certified ScrumMaster). After that comes the CSP-SM (Certified Scrum Professional - ScrumMaster). You renew your certification every 2 years by earning SEUs. Continuing to learn matters because the CSM is only a start; real skill comes from experience and practice.
